chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu Jameela, from Humayd al-Sayrafi, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
Every construction that is not complete (or has a boundary/limit), it is a burden/evil consequence for its owner on the Day of Resurrection.
ai.seo_question: What is the religious ruling on buildings without boundaries in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from al-Kafi is often interpreted through the lens of *kafaf* (sufficiency or enclosure), warning against architectural negligence that leads to ambiguity in property rights or spiritual clutter. Scholars like Al-Majlisi contextualize this as a principle of *adab* (etiquette) in habitation, where physical disorder reflects or causes spiritual burden (*wibal*), linking material stewardship to eschatological accountability.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Abu Jameela, from Humeyd Al Sayrafi, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Every construction without a boundary, so it would have bad consequences for its owner on the Day of Judgement’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from Safwan ibn Yahya from abu Jamilah from Hamid al- Sayrafiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
The constructions that are not within owner’s budget will be a burden for him on the Day of Judgment.’”
